summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a one-week history of burning epigastric pain, coffee-ground emesis, and melena, in the setting of chronic pancreatitis, Sjogren’s syndrome, and ongoing prednisone use for presumed vasculitis. Her symptoms differed from prior pancreatitis episodes, with no radiation to the back and normal lipase. Initial labs showed a drop in hemoglobin from 12.1 to 10.2 g/dL, suggesting gastrointestinal blood loss. She was managed with IV fluids, famotidine (due to IV PPI allergy), and pain control with Dilaudid. An endoscopy revealed normal mucosa in the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum with no active bleeding or ulcers. The proton pump inhibitor was increased to pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily. Her condition stabilized, pain improved, and she was discharged home on hospital day three with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology and to return if symptoms recurred.
problems: Dyspepsia and other specified disorders of function of stomach
